subject: Annual planning: budget targets & scenario mapping
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: leadership@redwood.com
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Annual planning: budget targets & scenario mapping

Team —

Kicking off annual planning and budget for FY26. Goal is to lock top-line targets and scenario assumptions so each org can complete their detailed budgets by Mar 15. High-level calendar attached. Please do the following this week: 

- Review the attached 2026_budget_template.xlsx and populate top-down revenue targets for your org by EOD Wed Mar 4. Include three scenario lines: Downside, Base, Upside.
- Flag any hires you believe are critical for the Base vs Upside scenarios.
- Note major one-time costs (licenses, vendor migrations, events).

I want a short memo from each org (1–2 paragraphs) describing the key upside risks and an ask if you need any upfront funding to hit Upside. We'll consolidate and present options to the exec team the week of Mar 22.

Planning_Timeline.pdf attached (draft).

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
VP, Strategy & Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 2026_budget_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 198 KB)
Attachment: Planning_Timeline.pdf (application/pdf, 120 KB)

To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: leadership@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual planning: budget targets & scenario mapping

Laura —

Thanks for the kickoff. Quick initial numbers from Sales for the top-down sheet (will fill the template tonight):

- Downside: $18.5M ARR (we assume 10% churn uptick, slower inbound)
- Base: $26.0M ARR (current funnel conversion, modest upsells)
- Upside: $34.2M ARR (faster ACV expansion + two enterprise closes)

Notes / questions:
- Do you want us to break the targets by channel (self-serve / PLG / enterprise) in the top-line sheet, or keep it consolidated? Channel-level assumptions drive GTM headcount requests.
- I'll attach a quick exports of our scenario pipeline: Sales_Conservative_Mid_Optimistic.csv.

Aditya
Head of Sales

Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -0800

Laura / Aditya —

Thanks for starting this. A couple of suggestions from Finance on scenario definitions and timeline so we can align headcount and cash planning: 

- Scenario definitions (proposal):
  * Downside — hiring pause after Q1, -15% revenue vs plan, 10–12% lower gross margin due to fixed infra costs.
  * Base — continue planned hiring (as currently approved), expected revenue per org as provided.
  * Upside — accelerated hiring, 20% higher revenue; plan for incremental $2.5M spend on go-to-market in Q2 to capture market share.

- Please annotate the template where hiring is assumed (FTE count and timing). We will run cash-flow runs for the Base/Downside/Upside and present results by Mar 10.

I've attached 2026_scenario_assumptions.docx with the financial levers and suggested default unit-costs. Also added a proposed meeting cadence in the doc — recommend Mar 8 for an initial cross-functional alignment meeting.

Markus
Director, Finance

Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual planning: budget targets & scenario mapping

Adding Product perspective —

High-level product drivers to bake into scenarios: 
- Model licensing & inference costs: if Upside demand grows, we should expect token volume to scale non-linearly; recommend separate line items for hosted vs dedicated/private deployments.
- Feature investment: deferred features (autoscaling, long-context evaluation tooling) could be deprioritized in Downside.
- Experimentation budget: keep a small central fund for platform experiments (~$250k in Base).

Attached Infra_cost_assumptions.pdf with per-region inference cost estimates (US/EU/APAC) and a rough calculation for dedicated pool growth. Will annotate the budget template with product-specific line items by Mar 4.

Evelyn
Head of Product

Attachment: Infra_cost_assumptions.pdf (application/pdf, 80 KB)

Laura / Markus —

Appreciate the invite to review. A few benchmarking notes from our portfolio (useful for sizing):
- Typical conversion uplift from dedicated offerings is ~12–18% within 12 months if the GTM motion is staffed (higher ARR impact in enterprise segments).
- Unit inference cost assumptions vary widely; we use the Greenfield Cost Index (link in doc) — if you’d like, I can share our cost model overlay.

Attached are two slides with suggested unit-cost ranges and a short note on expected CAC changes if you prioritize enterprise-led campaigns. Happy to join the Mar 8 cadence if that’s helpful.

Karen Ellis
Partner, Acme Analytics
